provenance:
ADR-029 §e's classification ruling under test: a LAYOUT table -- a bullet typeset as a 4-cell -- is recorded faithfully and is NOT filtered out as 'not a data table'. MSFT FY2013 10-K, the first bullet of Item 1's 'Windows Division' risk list, raw bytes [50620, 51146) of filing.htm (526 bytes; the 6th
of | | | . • is the cp1252 bullet, html.unescape maps it to U+2022 '•' per the HTML5 spec; the two  -only cells are ''. One row, four cells. Why this is the ruling and not an accident: msft-2013 has 178 recorded tables, 88 of them one row long; measured 2026-08-23 over the derived grids, 57 of those 88 are exactly this four-cell bullet shape (cell 1 is '•'), 29 are two-cell '(a)'/'(b)'/'*' footnote rows and the remaining 2 are the cover page's check-box rows -- so a third of this filing's tables are layout tables. A heuristic that dropped them would need a definition of 'data table' that no committed case could pin without a second, larger label set, and a false negative there is a silently missing table -- the silent-failure class this repo exists to refuse (INV-0, ADR-019). So the extractor does not classify: every

that carries visible text is a record; 'is it data?' is a consumer question answerable from the record itself (row count, numeric density) and the Markdown view renders it as the two-cell row it is. Anchor occurs once in the raw file and once in normalized_text. Measured at HEAD: record #5 of 178, normalized_text[11032:11125]. The table_markdown value is derived by hand from the labeled row under ADR-029 §b: columns 0 and 2 are empty and are not shown; a one-row table is a header row plus its separator and nothing else.
